classification.difficultyReason: Identify included angles from isosceles and equilateral properties, and combine two triangular areas for a parallelogram.

content.prompt: Calculate each area, correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle ABC, with AB and AC labelled 5.6 cm and an angle arc at B labelled 70 degrees. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Since $AB=AC$, the base angles at $B$ and $C$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle BAC&=40^\circ\\\text{Area of }ABC&=\tfrac12\times5.6\times5.6\sin40^\circ\\\text{Area of }ABC&\approx10.08\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of the whole parallelogram $ABCD$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with single parallel arrowheads on AD and BC, double parallel arrowheads on AB and DC, and a red dashed diagonal BD.
spec.mathematics: AB=5 cm, AD=10 cm, angle BAD=70 degrees; BD divides the parallelogram into equal-area triangles.

answer.worked:
Diagonal $BD$ divides the parallelogram into two triangles of equal area.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABD&=\tfrac12\times5\times10\sin70^\circ\\\text{Area of }ABCD&=2\times\tfrac12\times5\times10\sin70^\circ\\\text{Area of }ABCD&\approx46.98\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC with identical single equality ticks on all three sides; BC is labelled 10 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The inferred angle and calculated area are not visible.

answer.worked:
The three equal sides make $ABC$ equilateral, so each angle is $60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABC&=\tfrac12\times10\times10\sin60^\circ\\\text{Area of }ABC&=25\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2\\\text{Area of }ABC&\approx43.30\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Pages 28–29 derive the included-angle area rule and Example 18 substitutes two sides and their included angle, rounding only the final area. Pages 13–14 demonstrate triangle-angle sums and sine-rule working.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Each part assesses the triangle area rule after identifying an included angle or decomposing a parallelogram. The answer key confirms that part b requests the whole parallelogram.

answerEvidence.matchEvidence: The teacher image under Exercise 12H, Question 2, prints a 10.08 cm², b 46.98 cm² and c 43.30 cm². Student part a shows two 5.6 cm sides and a 70° base angle, giving included angle 40° and area 15.68 sin 40° = 10.0789… cm². Part b shows parallelogram sides 5 cm and 10 cm with included angle 70°, giving total area 50 sin 70° = 46.9846… cm². Part c shows three identical equality marks and a 10 cm side, giving area 50 sin 60° = 43.3012… cm². All three independently derived rounded values match the individually labelled key entries.
